response.answer: The GCV method is used to choose Tikhonov λ in SVD Δ-inversion for the primary BLP estimator. It balances regularization errors and perturbation effectively.

results.title: Multi-parameter Tikhonov regularization-based OTPA with application to ship-radiated noise evaluation | AIP Advances | AIP Publishing
results.content: The obtained results indicate that the average error of M-P Tikhonov regularization is reduced by up to 0.38 dB compared with that of the L-curve, 0.68 dB compared with that of the GCV, and 1.34 dB compared with that of the SVD under various combinations of noise levels, which can provide guidance for ship-radiated noise evaluation in engineering applications. Then, this paper analyzes the calculation methods for the regularization parameter, which involves the generalized cross validation (GCV)19,20 method and the L-curve criterion.21 The GCV seeks to balance the regularization errors and perturbation, and the L-curve is a plot of the norm of a regularized solution vs the norm of the corresponding residual, as the regularization parameter is varied.9 However, due to the environmental noise and ill-condition system, the L-curve criterion and GCV method still have deficiencies in the stability and anti-interference performance of the TF.22 Then, the M-P method can obtain the optimal regularization parameter by optimizing the GCV and L-curve methods based on the condition number,23,24 which can take into account both the stability and accuracy of the TF. Comparison of underwater noise pressure spectrum levels of operating conditions 8# and 30# and the condition number, where “Measured” represents the measured radiated noise, “L-curve” is the radiated noise evaluated by Tikhonov with the L-curve method, “GCV” is the radiated noise evaluated by Tikhonov with the GCV method, and “SVD” is the radiated noise evaluated by the SVD method. Cumulative errors in dB for the GCV, L-curve, and SVD methods under various combinations of noise levels for operating condition 8#. Cumulative errors in dB for the GCV, L-curve, and SVD methods under various combinations of noise levels for operating condition 30#. Meanwhile, the cumulative error when using the Tikhonov method with the L-curve is 0.36 dB less than the cumulative error using the GCV method under the high noise levels of operating condition 30#.
